---REDU.MD---
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/ENTERPILOT/GoModel
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: enterpilot/gomodel:0.1.77
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: gomodel
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔⛔ THIS GATEWAY HOLDS THE USER'S PROVIDER API KEYS, SO AN UNAUTHENTICATED ONE ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S BILL ON THEIR ACCOUNT. Set GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY in the compose environment BEFORE the first boot. If it is empty, internal/server/auth.go:42-47 lets EVERY request through, and internal/server/http.go:242-246 additionally appends /admin/* to the authentication skip list as a lockout-recovery path. Upstream states the consequence itself at docs/guides/production.mdx:158-161: an internet-reachable gateway in that state hands anyone the full admin API. Anyone who finds the hostname can then read every logged prompt, mint managed keys, and spend the user's OpenAI or Anthropic balance through the gateway. Generate 32 or more alphanumeric characters (alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in JSON or a shell), pass it at deploy time, and never write the value into this file or a compose committed anywhere."
  - "WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: nobody signs up, because GoModel has NO USER ACCOUNTS and no registration. Administration is holding GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY, and you set it as an environment variable at deploy time, which is the one ownership shape that is safe by construction: there is no window between the hostname going live and somebody claiming it, PROVIDED the variable is set on the first boot. There is therefore nothing to close afterwards. Further access is created inside the dashboard as managed API keys, each with its own dashboard_access flag; internal/server/auth.go:191-208 refuses a key without that flag with 403 on /admin/*. The master key always passes."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST REACHES ONCE THE KEY IS SET, read from the skip list at internal/server/http.go:222-252, because this is not obvious: GET /health and GET /health/ready always; /admin/dashboard, /admin/dashboard/* and /admin/static/* whenever the UI is enabled; /swagger/* when SWAGGER_ENABLED, WHICH DEFAULTS TO TRUE; /metrics when METRICS_ENABLED; /debug/pprof/* when PPROF_ENABLED. Everything else answers 401. The dashboard paths serve the SPA shell and its assets only, never data (docs/guides/production.mdx:347-351 says this is by design); the shell asks for the key and stores it in the browser, and every data call it makes is authenticated. So set SWAGGER_ENABLED=false, and leave METRICS_ENABLED and PPROF_ENABLED off unless the user asks: the upstream dev compose turns metrics ON, and that endpoint is unauthenticated by design."
  - "⛔ DO NOT USE THE UPSTREAM docker-compose.yaml. It is a development stack and it fails in three separate ways here. Its gomodel service BUILDS from source (docker-compose.yaml:5-10) rather than pulling the published image; that service and prometheus are both behind profiles: [app], so a plain docker compose up -d starts redis, postgres, mongodb and adminer AND NO GATEWAY AT ALL, which the file's own first two lines say out loud; and it publishes 5432, 27017, 6379 plus an unauthenticated adminer on 8081 and pins prom/prometheus:latest. Write a one-service compose from the pinned image instead. This entry's recipe does exactly that, and everything it needs is an environment variable."
  - "⛔ STORAGE_TYPE DEFAULTS TO SQLITE AND THE IMAGE DECLARES NO VOLUME, WHICH IS THE COMBINATION THAT LOSES EVERYTHING QUIETLY. config/storage.go:60-62 falls back to sqlite when the variable is empty, and docs/guides/production.mdx:69-75 spells out the rest: the default path resolves to /app/data/gomodel.db, an image-layer directory, so at the next container replacement every audit log, usage record, budget, MANAGED API KEY and stored provider credential is gone, with a perfectly healthy container throughout. Set STORAGE_TYPE=postgresql and POSTGRES_URL and point them at redu's managed Postgres."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE IS NOT EVIDENCE. Over SSH on the app VM, first find the container and REFUSE TO CONTINUE if you cannot (a grep that never ran returns zero matches and reads as a pass): C=$(sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i gomodel | head -1). Then the POSITIVE half, which is also what proves your command reached the app at all: sudo docker logs \"$C\" 2>&1 | grep 'storage configured' | grep -c postgresql must be 1 or more. Only then the NEGATIVE halves: the same pipeline ending grep -c sqlite must be 0, and sudo docker logs \"$C\" 2>&1 | grep -c 'UNSAFE MODE' must be 0. Those exact strings are at internal/app/app.go:1137-1141 and 1123-1125. Logs are JSON because stdout is not a TTY. Note the VM runs docker, not podman."
  - "DATABASE WIRING, EXACTLY. deploy_compose only APPENDS PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD and DATABASE_URL to the project .env and never edits your compose, so your compose has to build the URL itself. GoModel reads neither DATABASE_URL nor the individual PG variables: it reads POSTGRES_URL only. Interpolate it as postgres://${PGUSER}:[REDACTED:conn-password]@${PGHOST}:${PGPORT}/${PGDATABASE}?sslmode=require and set sslmode deliberately, since pgx defaults to prefer, which will silently accept an unencrypted connection. GoModel wants exactly ONE database (internal/storage/postgresql.go:17-47 is a pool against an existing one), so redu's one-database-per-managed-Postgres rule never bites here, and db_superuser is NOT needed: it creates its tables inside the database redu provisions."
  - "⛔ THERE IS NO ENCRYPTION KEY, AND THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS. Unlike most entries in this library there is no secret whose loss destroys stored data. GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY is a constant-time compare against the environment value (internal/server/auth.go:78-82) and is stored nowhere, so what a changed key destroys on a redeploy is ACCESS: every client configured with the old one starts failing, all at once, with no data loss to warn you. Reuse the same value on every redeploy. The other half is worse and is the reason to care about the database: docs/guides/production.mdx:113-119 says provider credentials saved through the DASHBOARD are written to provider_credentials AS PLAINTEXT, with no encryption at rest, and the *** masking is applied on the read path only. Treat the managed Postgres, its backups and its snapshots as credential material."
  - "DECLARE PROVIDER API KEYS AS ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES, NOT THROUGH THE DASHBOARD, and the second reason is the one people miss. Per docs/guides/production.mdx:100-126: credentials declared in env or config.yaml are never written to the store at all; and a provider row that lives in the database can be edited by ANYONE holding a dashboard-capable key, INCLUDING its base_url, which silently repoints every prompt and the injected upstream key at a host of their choosing. Env-declared providers are read-only in the dashboard, so that change can only arrive through a redeploy. Put OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and friends in the compose environment, ask the user for the values at deploy time, and NEVER write a value into this file."
  - "PORT 8080, from Dockerfile:47 (EXPOSE 8080); the PORT variable overrides it and you should leave it alone. Point health checks at GET /health/ready, NOT /health: internal/server/handlers.go:475-477 shows /health checks nothing at all and returns {\"status\":\"ok\"} whatever the state of the database, while internal/server/readiness.go:52-83 probes storage, answers 503 when it is down, and returns {\"status\":\"ready\",\"components\":{\"storage\":\"ok\"}}. Also note the image is distroless with no shell and no curl, so a container healthcheck written with curl can never succeed; the binary probes itself with /gomodel --health, which is what the upstream Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK uses."
  - "LOGGING_LOG_BODIES DEFAULTS TO TRUE, WHICH IS A PRIVACY DECISION AND A DISK DECISION AT THE SAME TIME. docs/guides/production.mdx:296-310: full request and response bodies are stored with no content redaction, up to about 2 MB per request, retained for LOGGING_RETENTION_DAYS (default 30). So everything anyone types into a prompt sits in the database for a month, and on a managed Postgres at m1.small with 20 GB of disk this is the single thing that fills it. Put that to the user before deploying and set LOGGING_LOG_BODIES=false for a metadata-only audit trail if they would rather. Credential HEADERS are redacted on the write path either way."
  - "⚠️ COST TRACKING AND BUDGETS DEPEND ON ONE OUTBOUND FETCH, AND ITS FAILURE IS SILENT. docs/guides/production.mdx:182-208: model pricing comes from the metadata registry at MODEL_LIST_URL, fetched in the background at startup. When it fails the gateway boots normally and /health and /health/ready still return 200; what you lose is pricing, so cost tracking reports no cost and BUDGETS HAVE NOTHING TO CHARGE AGAINST AND WILL NOT ENFORCE SPEND LIMITS. If a user is relying on budgets as their spend guard, verify a model shows a price in the dashboard before telling them they are protected. Setting MODEL_LIST_URL to an empty string does NOT disable the fetch, because empty environment values are skipped when overrides are applied."
  - "NO TLS AND NO CORS IN THE APP. docs/guides/production.mdx:163-171: GoModel serves plain HTTP and expects a reverse proxy in front, which is exactly what redu's hostname provides, so this is handled. But there is NO CORS middleware at all, so a browser application on another origin cannot call the gateway directly. Server-side callers and the SDKs are unaffected. Do not promise a user browser-side access without adding those headers at a proxy."
  - "PIN THE IMAGE FROM THE REGISTRY: enterpilot/gomodel:0.1.77, published 2026-08-16, confirmed present in the Docker Hub tag list for enterpilot/gomodel. A latest tag does exist on this one, unlike some projects, which makes it easy to write by habit and wrong to: the project ships releases most days, so an unpinned redeploy crosses several versions of a gateway your users' agents depend on. Pin it, and read the release notes before moving it."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND THE ONLY RAM FIGURE THAT EXISTS IS UPSTREAM'S OWN. docs/guides/production.mdx:21-26 quotes their benchmarks page: a 16 MB compressed image, 37 MB peak RAM under load, 0.56 s cold start. That is THEIR measurement on THEIR hardware, not one redu has reproduced. m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is reasoning from that plus Dockerfile:36 (CGO_ENABLED=0 static binary on distroless, no interpreter, no runtime dependencies). The load that would move it is concurrent streaming and the audit buffer, not the binary. Measure it on your run and write the number back rather than repeating this paragraph."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.035/hr, roughly GBP 25 a month; fits the no-card free trial) AND the provider-key question, and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 8080. Pass flavor_id explicitly: plan_deploy upsizes compose stacks once needs_compose is declared, and this one is a single 16 MB static binary that does not need it."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source; cloning the upstream monorepo would fetch a 31 MB tree to run a published image. Write the one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."

YOU CAN READ A DEPLOY VM WITHOUT SSHING INTO IT, and four tools do it: get_containers (what is running, health, restarts, crashed ones included), get_container_logs (what the app actually printed - the tool for 'deployed fine but does not work'), get_resource_usage (memory, disk, load, OOM kills) and get_env_keys (which variables got wired, by name). ⛔ get_instance_logs is the SERIAL CONSOLE and is not your app's logs; build_log stops when the build does. SSH is still yours for everything else - a shell on a real machine is the point, not a fallback. ⭐ MEASURED over 38 deploys: of 241 ssh escapes, 146 (61%) were exactly these four things, and the four tools were called 11 times. They are faster than a login, they cost the VM nothing extra (the reading is already cached), and reaching for ssh to run `docker ps` is the single most common wasted minute in a deploy.

⛔ THE PRIMARY SURFACE'S HOSTNAME COMES FROM THE TOP-LEVEL dname, NOT FROM expose[0].dname, WHICH IS SILENTLY DISCARDED. Extra expose entries DO keep the dname you give them, so the two behave differently and nothing tells you. If an app bakes its own public URL into config at boot (CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN, allowed_origins, SITE_URL), generate the full `<label>-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud` form yourself and pass it as the TOP-LEVEL dname, which is used verbatim. Passing it on expose[0] instead gets you an app configured for a hostname redu never created, answering 200 on a name it does not believe is its own.

WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH THE PROXY WITH NO CONFIGURATION: every proxy host redu creates has upgrade enabled. Measured at the protocol level, HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols with the subprotocol echoed back. ⚠️ TEST IT WITH `curl --http1.1`: plain curl negotiates HTTP/2, which has no Upgrade mechanism at all, so the app answers as an ordinary GET and the failure looks exactly like a proxy refusing to upgrade. Browsers use HTTP/1.1 for websockets regardless. Do not disable an app's realtime features on the strength of an HTTP/2 curl.

input.redu_md:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/ENTERPILOT/GoModel
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: enterpilot/gomodel:0.1.77
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: gomodel
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔⛔ THIS GATEWAY HOLDS THE USER'S PROVIDER API KEYS, SO AN UNAUTHENTICATED ONE ON A PUBLIC HOSTNAME IS SOMEBODY ELSE'S BILL ON THEIR ACCOUNT. Set GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY in the compose environment BEFORE the first boot. If it is empty, internal/server/auth.go:42-47 lets EVERY request through, and internal/server/http.go:242-246 additionally appends /admin/* to the authentication skip list as a lockout-recovery path. Upstream states the consequence itself at docs/guides/production.mdx:158-161: an internet-reachable gateway in that state hands anyone the full admin API. Anyone who finds the hostname can then read every logged prompt, mint managed keys, and spend the user's OpenAI or Anthropic balance through the gateway. Generate 32 or more alphanumeric characters (alphanumeric only, so there is nothing to escape in JSON or a shell), pass it at deploy time, and never write the value into this file or a compose committed anywhere."
  - "WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: nobody signs up, because GoModel has NO USER ACCOUNTS and no registration. Administration is holding GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY, and you set it as an environment variable at deploy time, which is the one ownership shape that is safe by construction: there is no window between the hostname going live and somebody claiming it, PROVIDED the variable is set on the first boot. There is therefore nothing to close afterwards. Further access is created inside the dashboard as managed API keys, each with its own dashboard_access flag; internal/server/auth.go:191-208 refuses a key without that flag with 403 on /admin/*. The master key always passes."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST REACHES ONCE THE KEY IS SET, read from the skip list at internal/server/http.go:222-252, because this is not obvious: GET /health and GET /health/ready always; /admin/dashboard, /admin/dashboard/* and /admin/static/* whenever the UI is enabled; /swagger/* when SWAGGER_ENABLED, WHICH DEFAULTS TO TRUE; /metrics when METRICS_ENABLED; /debug/pprof/* when PPROF_ENABLED. Everything else answers 401. The dashboard paths serve the SPA shell and its assets only, never data (docs/guides/production.mdx:347-351 says this is by design); the shell asks for the key and stores it in the browser, and every data call it makes is authenticated. So set SWAGGER_ENABLED=false, and leave METRICS_ENABLED and PPROF_ENABLED off unless the user asks: the upstream dev compose turns metrics ON, and that endpoint is unauthenticated by design."
  - "⛔ DO NOT USE THE UPSTREAM docker-compose.yaml. It is a development stack and it fails in three separate ways here. Its gomodel service BUILDS from source (docker-compose.yaml:5-10) rather than pulling the published image; that service and prometheus are both behind profiles: [app], so a plain docker compose up -d starts redis, postgres, mongodb and adminer AND NO GATEWAY AT ALL, which the file's own first two lines say out loud; and it publishes 5432, 27017, 6379 plus an unauthenticated adminer on 8081 and pins prom/prometheus:latest. Write a one-service compose from the pinned image instead. This entry's recipe does exactly that, and everything it needs is an environment variable."
  - "⛔ STORAGE_TYPE DEFAULTS TO SQLITE AND THE IMAGE DECLARES NO VOLUME, WHICH IS THE COMBINATION THAT LOSES EVERYTHING QUIETLY. config/storage.go:60-62 falls back to sqlite when the variable is empty, and docs/guides/production.mdx:69-75 spells out the rest: the default path resolves to /app/data/gomodel.db, an image-layer directory, so at the next container replacement every audit log, usage record, budget, MANAGED API KEY and stored provider credential is gone, with a perfectly healthy container throughout. Set STORAGE_TYPE=postgresql and POSTGRES_URL and point them at redu's managed Postgres."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE IS NOT EVIDENCE. Over SSH on the app VM, first find the container and REFUSE TO CONTINUE if you cannot (a grep that never ran returns zero matches and reads as a pass): C=$(sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i gomodel | head -1). Then the POSITIVE half, which is also what proves your command reached the app at all: sudo docker logs \"$C\" 2>&1 | grep 'storage configured' | grep -c postgresql must be 1 or more. Only then the NEGATIVE halves: the same pipeline ending grep -c sqlite must be 0, and sudo docker logs \"$C\" 2>&1 | grep -c 'UNSAFE MODE' must be 0. Those exact strings are at internal/app/app.go:1137-1141 and 1123-1125. Logs are JSON because stdout is not a TTY. Note the VM runs docker, not podman."
  - "DATABASE WIRING, EXACTLY. deploy_compose only APPENDS PGHOST, PGPORT, PGDATABASE, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD and DATABASE_URL to the project .env and never edits your compose, so your compose has to build the URL itself. # Self-host GoModel on redu

One OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible endpoint in front of every model provider you use,
with usage analytics, cost tracking, budgets, guardrails and a real-time audit log. A single
distroless Go container, a managed Postgres beside it, and a public HTTPS URL.

About GBP 0.035/hour, roughly GBP 25 a month. Inside the no-card free trial.

## What this deploys

- **GoModel** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 8080.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the audit log, usage records, budgets and
  managed API keys, so they survive every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS in front of it.
- A master key you set at deploy time, which is the only thing that owns this instance.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy GoModel on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Read this before you deploy: the gateway holds your provider keys

GoModel is a proxy that injects **your** OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or Groq credentials into every
request it forwards. That makes an unauthenticated one on a public hostname materially worse than
most self-hosted apps: it is not a leaked notebook, it is your provider bill, spendable by anyone
who finds the URL.

There are no user accounts and no signup, so nothing needs closing after the fact. **Whoever holds
`GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY` is the administrator**, and you set it as an environment variable before the
first boot. Set it and the ownership question is answered by construction. Leave it empty and the
gateway allows every request through, and adds `/admin/*` to its own authentication skip list as
a lockout-recovery path. Upstream documents that state as handing anyone the full admin API.

Two decisions to make with whoever you are deploying for:

- **Where do the provider keys live?** Declare them as environment variables. Keys saved through
  the dashboard are stored in the database in plaintext, and a database-stored provider can have
  its `base_url` edited by anyone with dashboard access, which silently redirects every prompt
  and the injected upstream key somewhere else.
- **Do you want full prompt bodies in the audit log?** `LOGGING_LOG_BODIES` defaults to on and
  keeps complete prompts and responses for 30 days. Excellent for debugging, and it is both the
  main driver of database growth and the reason anything sensitive typed into a prompt persists.

## The three that actually break it

**The upstream compose.** Its gateway service builds from source and sits behind a
`profiles: [app]` gate, so a plain `docker compose up -d` starts four databases and an
unauthenticated Adminer and **no gateway at all**. This recipe ships a one-service compose against
the published image instead.

**The storage default.** `STORAGE_TYPE` falls back to SQLite, and the image declares no volume,
so the database lands in an image-layer directory. The container is healthy the whole time and
every audit record, budget and managed API key disappears at the next replacement.

**The metadata fetch.** Model pricing comes from one outbound call. If it fails the gateway boots
normally and reports ready, but nothing has a price, so cost tracking shows zero and **budgets
stop enforcing spend limits**. If a user is relying on budgets as their guard, confirm a model
shows a price before telling them they are protected.

## Proving it is actually locked down

Run this after the deploy, with the master key in your shell. It refuses to answer rather than
answering wrongly: redu's hostname serves 502 for roughly the first 2.5 minutes while the
container starts, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" assertion.

```bash
set -u
HOST="$1"                       # gomodel-<generated>.redu.cloud
KEY="${GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY:-}"
INCONCLUSIVE=3

if [ -z "$KEY" ]; then
  echo "GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY is not set in this shell, so this check cannot tell" >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

body=$(mktemp)
code=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/health/ready")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "502 from the edge: still starting, re-run in a minute" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "readiness answered $code, not 200; cannot tell" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if ! grep -q '"status":"ready"' "$body"; then
  echo "no GoModel readiness body at /health/ready; cannot tell" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
rm -f "$body"

# POSITIVE half first: the master key reaches the admin API. This proves the route
# exists and that the negative check below is talking to GoModel at all.
ok=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://$HOST/admin/runtime/config")
if [ "$ok" = "404" ]; then
  echo "GET /admin/runtime/config is 404: the route moved, this check proves nothing" >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$ok" != "200" ]; then
  echo "the master key did not reach the admin API (HTTP $ok)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# NEGATIVE half, meaningful only because the line above returned 200.
anon=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin/runtime/config")
if [ "$anon" != "401" ]; then
  echo "ANONYMOUS admin access returned $anon, expected 401." >&2
  echo "Do not leave this instance running." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK: ready, master key authenticates, anonymous admin refused with 401"
```

And on the VM itself, for the storage question, again with the positive half first so the zeros
below it mean something:

```bash
set -u
C=$(sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i gomodel | head -1)
if [ -z "$C" ]; then
  echo "no gomodel container found: every grep below would be vacuously zero" >&2
  exit 3
fi

sudo docker logs "$C" 2>&1 | grep 'storage configured' | grep -c postgresql   # must be >= 1
sudo docker logs "$C" 2>&1 | grep 'storage configured' | grep -c sqlite       # must be 0
sudo docker logs "$C" 2>&1 | grep -c 'UNSAFE MODE'                            # must be 0
```

# GoModel gateway — one service, pulled from the pinned published image.

services:
  gomodel:
    image: enterpilot/gomodel:0.1.77
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      # Ownership. Empty here means GoModel authenticates nothing AND adds /admin/*

      GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY: "${GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY}"

      # with no declared volume: everything is lost at the next container replacement,

      # DATABASE_URL, not the individual PG* vars — so the URL is built here.
      # sslmode=require is explicit because pgx defaults to `prefer`, which will

      STORAGE_TYPE: "postgresql"

      SWAGGER_ENABLED: "false"

KEY="${GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY:-}"

if [ -z "$KEY" ]; then
  echo "GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY is not set in this shell, so this check cannot tell" >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

body=$(mktemp)
code=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/health/ready")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "502 from the edge: still starting, re-run in a minute" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "readiness answered $code, not 200; cannot tell" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if ! grep -q '"status":"ready"' "$body"; then
  echo "no GoModel readiness body at /health/ready; cannot tell" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
echo "readiness body: $(cat "$body")"
rm -f "$body"

ok=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://$HOST/admin/runtime/config")
if [ "$ok" = "404" ]; then
  echo "GET /admin/runtime/config is 404: the route moved, this check proves nothing" >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$ok" != "200" ]; then
  echo "the master key did not reach the admin API (HTTP $ok)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

anon=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin/runtime/config")
if [ "$anon" != "401" ]; then
  echo "ANONYMOUS admin access returned $anon, expected 401." >&2
  echo "Do not leave this instance running." >&2
  exit 1

# Self-host GoModel on redu

One OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible endpoint in front of every model provider you use,
with usage analytics, cost tracking, budgets, guardrails and a real-time audit log. A single
distroless Go container, a managed Postgres beside it, and a public HTTPS URL.

About GBP 0.035/hour, roughly GBP 25 a month. Inside the no-card free trial.

## What this deploys

- **GoModel** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 8080.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the audit log, usage records, budgets and
  managed API keys, so they survive every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS in front of it.
- A master key you set at deploy time, which is the only thing that owns this instance.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy GoModel on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Read this before you deploy: the gateway holds your provider keys

GoModel is a proxy that injects **your** OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or Groq credentials into every
request it forwards. That makes an unauthenticated one on a public hostname materially worse than
most self-hosted apps: it is not a leaked notebook, it is your provider bill, spendable by anyone
who finds the URL.

There are no user accounts and no signup, so nothing needs closing after the fact. **Whoever holds
`GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY` is the administrator**, and you set it as an environment variable before the
first boot. Set it and the ownership question is answered by construction. Leave it empty and the
gateway allows every request through, and adds `/admin/*` to its own authentication skip list as
a lockout-recovery path. Upstream documents that state as handing anyone the full admin API.

Two decisions to make with whoever you are deploying for:

- **Where do the provider keys live?** Declare them as environment variables. Keys saved through
  the dashboard are stored in the database in plaintext, and a database-stored provider can have
  its `base_url` edited by anyone with dashboard access, which silently redirects every prompt
  and the injected upstream key somewhere else.
- **Do you want full prompt bodies in the audit log?** `LOGGING_LOG_BODIES` defaults to on and
  keeps complete prompts and responses for 30 days. Excellent for debugging, and it is both the
  main driver of database growth and the reason anything sensitive typed into a prompt persists.

## The three that actually break it

**The upstream compose.** Its gateway service builds from source and sits behind a
`profiles: [app]` gate, so a plain `docker compose up -d` starts four databases and an
unauthenticated Adminer and **no gateway at all**. This recipe ships a one-service compose against
the published image instead.

**The storage default.** `STORAGE_TYPE` falls back to SQLite, and the image declares no volume,
so the database lands in an image-layer directory. The container is healthy the whole time and
every audit record, budget and managed API key disappears at the next replacement.

**The metadata fetch.** Model pricing comes from one outbound call. If it fails the gateway boots
normally and reports ready, but nothing has a price, so cost tracking shows zero and **budgets
stop enforcing spend limits**. If a user is relying on budgets as their guard, confirm a model
shows a price before telling them they are protected.

## Proving it is actually locked down

Run this after the deploy, with the master key in your shell. It refuses to answer rather than
answering wrongly: redu's hostname serves 000 then 502 for roughly the first 3.5 minutes while the
VM is created and the container starts, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" assertion.

```bash
set -u
HOST="$1"                       # gomodel-<generated>.redu.cloud
KEY="${GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY:-}"
INCONCLUSIVE=3

if [ -z "$KEY" ]; then
  echo "GOMODEL_MASTER_KEY is not set in this shell, so this check cannot tell" >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi

body=$(mktemp)
code=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/health/ready")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "502 from the edge: still starting, re-run in a minute" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "readiness answered $code, not 200; cannot tell" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if ! grep -q '"status":"ready"' "$body"; then
  echo "no GoModel readiness body at /health/ready; cannot tell" >&2
  rm -f "$body"; exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
rm -f "$body"

# POSITIVE half first: the master key reaches the admin API. This proves the route
# exists and that the negative check below is talking to GoModel at all.
ok=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://$HOST/admin/runtime/config")
if [ "$ok" = "404" ]; then
  echo "GET /admin/runtime/config is 404: the route moved, this check proves nothing" >&2
  exit "$INCONCLUSIVE"
fi
if [ "$ok" != "200" ]; then
  echo "the master key did not reach the admin API (HTTP $ok)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# NEGATIVE half, meaningful only because the line above returned 200.
anon=$(curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin/runtime/config")
if [ "$anon" != "401" ]; then
  echo "ANONYMOUS admin access returned $anon, expected 401." >&2
  echo "Do not leave this instance running." >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "OK: ready, master key authenticates, anonymous admin refused with 401"
```

And on the VM itself, for the storage question, again with the positive half first so the zeros
below it mean something:

```bash
set -u
C=$(sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i gomodel | head -1)
if [ -z "$C" ]; then
  echo "no gomodel container found: every grep below would be vacuously zero" >&2
  exit 3
fi

sudo docker logs "$C" 2>&1 | grep 'storage configured' | grep -c postgresql   # must be >= 1
sudo docker logs "$C" 2>&1 | grep 'storage configured' | grep -c sqlite       # must be 0
sudo docker logs "$C" 2>&1 | grep -c 'UNSAFE MODE'                            # must be 0
```
